market.headline: Nvidia beat forecasts last night and US futures are up this morning, but rates are still high and the S&P 500 sits at a five-month low.
points: Chips: Nvidia's sales doubled from a year ago to about $116 billion, and it expects about $130 billion next quarter, more than analysts hoped. The stock rose about 4% before the open, and AMD and Broadcom gained 2% to 3%. The new US chip export rules still take effect on Thursday.

Tuesday: The S&P 500 fell 1% for its fourth loss in a row, and the Dow dropped about 850 points. Software stocks were hit hard (Salesforce fell 9%) on fears that AI tools will replace their products. Health stocks also slid after the US proposed new anti-fraud rules for Medicare and Medicaid.

Rates: The 10-year US bond yield is about 5.1%. Traders now expect the Fed to raise rates in December because inflation is running hot. Higher rates usually weigh on pricey growth stocks and on home spending.

Events: The Fed's meeting notes come out at 2 pm Eastern today. Anthropic prices its IPO tonight and starts trading Thursday. P&G holds its investor day Thursday, and Microsoft's outage report is due Friday.
market.plan: Nvidia cleared its big test, but one good morning does not fix the trend. Keep any new buys small, favour the calm names and the halal funds, and give chips and software a few days to settle.

stocks.sum: The simple, certified way to own about 220 halal US companies at once.
why: About 10% below its high after four down days, so you are not buying at the top.
One purchase spreads your money over many companies, so one bad stock hurts less.
Certified halal, so there is no screening homework.
risk: Nvidia and Apple are a big part of the fund, so big tech news moves it a lot.
The market is still falling day to day and rates are high, so it could slip more before it turns.
stocks.todo: Still the best first purchase on this list. Nvidia's results are out, so you can add the second piece now, or spread it over a couple of weeks if the swings bother you.

stocks.sum: A calm, Canadian-dollar halal fund. No currency fee when you buy it.
why: Trades in Canadian dollars, so you skip the 1.5% US currency fee each way.
Holds steady companies around the world and moves much less than tech.
Certified halal.
risk: Slow mover. Good for safety, weak for quick gains.

I could not confirm a dated close after Nov 13, so the price shown is from then. Wealthsimple's page showed about $36.90 but with no date, which would be a little lower. Check the live price in the app.
stocks.todo: A sensible place for money you can't afford to see swing, like a down payment. Check the live price first and use a limit order.

stocks.sum: A halal income fund that pays monthly, about 4.9% a year. Not a growth play.
why: Pays a small amount every month.
Barely moves when stocks drop. It even ticked up a little on Tuesday.
risk: It sits less than 1% above its 52-week low of $17.30. With the Fed likely to raise rates in December, funds like this can drift lower.
US withholding tax takes 15% of the payouts inside an FHSA.
stocks.todo: Only use it to park cash for income. It will not help a few-month profit goal.

stocks.earnNote: Broadcom, a big holding, reports Dec 9
stocks.sum: The chip rebound trade without leverage, spread over 26 chip makers.
why: About 32% below its high, so there is real room to recover.
Nvidia's strong results lifted chip stocks before the open, and this fund spreads you across all of them.
risk: It moves almost twice as much as the market. It closed down 0.4% Tuesday before Nvidia's results came out.
The new US chip export rules start Thursday, and the Anthropic IPO will test how much money is still chasing AI.
stocks.todo: Let Nvidia's bounce and the new chip rules settle for a few days. If chips hold their gains into next week, think about one share.

stocks.sum: The AI chip leader. Strong results last night, but big questions about who runs it.
why: Sales doubled from a year ago, and next quarter's forecast beat what analysts expected.
About 36% below its high, and cheap against its expected profits. It rose about 4% before Wednesday's open.
risk: The board says it will not bring back Jensen Huang, and there are reports of government probes tied to his exit. A permanent CEO is still not named.
It moves more than twice as much as the market, so a one-day jump can fade fast.
The new US rules on chip sales to Chinese firms abroad start Thursday.
stocks.todo: Good news, but let it settle. Watch a few days of trading and any CEO news before buying.

stocks.sum: A big winner from custom AI chips, about 31% below its high.
why: It rose 2.5% on Tuesday, one of the few gainers, and was up again before Wednesday's open after Nvidia's results.
Analysts' average target is well above the price.
risk: Its own earnings on Dec 9 are the next big test, about three weeks away.
The new US chip rules start Thursday and could hit the whole group.
stocks.todo: Wait a few days for the chip rules to kick in. If you buy, plan to be out or smaller before Dec 9.

stocks.sum: Strong business, but the wildest stock on this list.
why: Record quarter on Nov 3, and it rose about 3% before Wednesday's open after Nvidia's results.
risk: It moves two and a half times as much as the market, and it fell almost 9% on Friday and almost 6% on Monday before steadying Tuesday.
Singapore was about 12% of its sales last year, so the new US licence rules for Southeast Asia, starting Thursday, are a direct risk.
Very expensive against current profits, so bad news hits it hard.
stocks.todo: Skip it for now. A normal stop can't protect you well on a stock that swings this much.

stocks.sum: Makes the chips for nearly every AI company, so it wins whoever leads.
why: About 26% below its high, and it just reported a record month of sales.
Nvidia's strong forecast is good news for TSMC, since it makes Nvidia's chips.
risk: It fell another 3.7% on Tuesday, its fourth drop in a row.
Taiwan and US-China politics are a standing risk, and the new US chip rules start Thursday.
stocks.todo: Wait until the chip rules take effect and the price stops falling, then consider one share.

stocks.sum: The steady one in tech, but software stocks are under pressure this week.
why: About 9% below its high, a smaller drop than most of tech.
Moves about the same as the market, so the stop can be tighter.
Its own earnings are already out, so no company surprise is due soon.
risk: It fell 2.3% on Tuesday as software stocks sold off on fears that AI tools will replace some software. That is its second down day in a row.
Microsoft's final report on last week's outage is due Nov 20.
One share is about $720 CAD, a big piece of a small account.
stocks.todo: Changed from buy to wait. Let the software selloff and Friday's outage report pass. If it steadies next week, a limit order for one share is fair.

stocks.sum: The cheapest big tech name against its profits, about 31% below its high.
why: Its price-to-earnings is near 15, which is low for a big tech company. That means you pay less for each dollar of profit.
Its income comes from ads and cloud, so it depends less on chip spending.
Its own earnings are already out.
risk: It fell another 1.2% on Tuesday. It plans to buy about $10 billion of Anthropic shares alongside the IPO, and investors worry about heavy AI spending.
Anthropic prices tonight and starts trading Thursday. A strong or weak debut could move Alphabet too.
It sits only about 3.5% above its 52-week low. Cheap stocks can get cheaper.
stocks.todo: Let the Anthropic debut pass on Thursday, then look at buying one share if the price holds above its low.

stocks.sum: A safe haven lately, but priced at the top.
why: Investors moved into Apple while chips fell. It barely moved on Tuesday.
risk: It sits about 2.5% below its all-time high and above analysts' average target.
Pricey against profits, so there is little room left for a few-month trade.
stocks.todo: Hold off. Put it on your list for a pullback of 8% or more.

stocks.sum: A story stock. The price runs on headlines more than on profits.
why: About 24% below its high, and it is pushing ahead with its Cybercab robotaxi.
risk: Extremely expensive against its profits.
It swings on headlines, like talk of a SpaceX merger and weak China sales in October.
stocks.todo: Skip for a planned, rule-based trade. Too unpredictable.

stocks.sum: Reasonably priced and about 21% below its high, but the halal status needs your own check.
why: Fair price against profits, and analysts' target is well above today's price.
risk: Halal screeners do not all agree on Meta. Check Zoya or Musaffa first.
It fell 1.2% on Tuesday and is borrowing heavily to pay for AI. Italy's privacy watchdog also fined it about 805 million euros.
The Anthropic IPO this week could shift money around in big tech.
stocks.todo: Settle the halal question first. If it passes for you, look again after the Anthropic debut.

stocks.sum: The weight-loss drug leader, about 3% below a record high.
why: Not a tech stock, so it spreads your risk.
It barely moves with the market.
risk: Near its high and close to analysts' average target, so the easy gains are behind it.
Health stocks slid Tuesday on proposed Medicare and Medicaid rules. It fell 1.1%.
One share costs about $2,010 CAD.
stocks.todo: Hold off. Too big for one share on a $10,000 account, and no real discount.

stocks.sum: A defensive stock that investors ran to during the tech selloff.
why: Very calm. It hardly reacts to market drops.
risk: About 3% below its high and right at analysts' average target, so you would be buying after the run.
It fell about 1.4% Tuesday with other health stocks, and the talc lawsuits are still ongoing.
stocks.todo: Hold off. Good company, wrong price for a new trade.

stocks.sum: A calm health care name about 21% below its high, but it slipped this week.
why: A discount without tech's wild swings.
Steady product news, like a new heart device lead approved in the US.
A low share price means you can buy several shares and size the trade exactly.
risk: It fell 2.5% on Tuesday, when health care was one of the weakest groups after the US proposed new Medicare and Medicaid anti-fraud rules.
Health stocks can stay out of favour for a long time.
stocks.todo: Changed from buy to wait. Give health stocks a few days to settle after the new rule news, then buy in one go if the price steadies.

why: People buy its products in any economy, and it just raised its dividend for the 70th year in a row.
risk: It closed at a new high of about $173 on Monday and is less than 1% below it now.
Its investor day is Thursday, Nov 19, which can move the price.
stocks.todo: Hold off. Useful as a safe corner later, not as a profit trade now.

stocks.sum: Beat forecasts on Tuesday and named a new CEO, but the stock fell 2.5%.
why: Sales and profit came in a little above forecasts, and it kept its full-year plan.
Fair price against profits, and older US homes need repairs.
risk: Fewer shoppers came in, even though each one spent more. Lowe's also reports today, which can move it.
The finance chief, Richard McPhail, takes over as CEO on Nov 23. Leadership changes can bring new plans and surprises.
High interest rates slow home sales and big renovation jobs, and a December rate hike looks likely.

stocks.sum: Sells gases that factories and hospitals need every day. Quiet and steady.
why: About 6% below its high and calmer than the market.
It has raised its dividend for decades, which signals a stable business.
Nothing to do with the AI trade, so it spreads your risk.
